  Case No.:      1924 05102023                     05-10-2023                          11-10-2023
                                    Report:                        Resolution:

   Location:        Lo Barnechea       Region:      Metropolitana     Classification:      Resolved.

                Reported what was described as a sphere, no size indicated,
Summary:
                that the user associated with the "morning star."

The user reported as follows: "I hope not to waste your time investigating something that turns out to be 'normal', but I provide you with a Report of the observation of an object (to me) unknown and inexplicable. From the outset, I inform you that my first impression was that I was observing Venus (the morning star) given the observation time, before dawn, and the observation direction (towards").

In the east, over the mountain range, that I have dismissed in principle since the characteristics of what was observed do not resemble what I expected to see from a planet. Perhaps it is due to the rudimentary nature of my observation instrument or something else easily explainable to you. I observed the object this morning, Thursday, October 5, 2023, starting just before 6:00 AM.

The photos were taken in a 75-degree east direction, at approximately 860 meters above sea level. In a clear, but still dark sky, no stars were visible, and I saw a very bright object, which appeared stationary, over the mountain range. I took pictures of it with my Samsung A33 5G smartphone, which has a night photography mode and a 10x optical zoom telephoto lens.

Description

User/a: I attach the photographic sequence, in which, as you will see, the file names contain the date and time of the photo's capture as follows.

File
20231005_060422. Photo taken on 2023 10 05 at 06:04:22

The first photo was taken from inside my house with constructions in the foreground, which allows for the precise determination of the capture point, if necessary.

It was necessary to recreate it, with, with the object observed in the image.

Then I performed a sequence of shots of the object with the telephoto lens at its maximum (10x) where it is observed that it is changing shape.

The last photo of the object, taken at 06:29, was taken with higher resolution (1.2 MB) allowing it to be seen enlarged with greater clarity.

The last photo in the sequence, which was taken half an hour after the

First, it shows a clearer sky, as it is 6:30 AM, and when compared to the first one, it appears that the object has moved up and to the left.

More details can be obtained about each image by accessing the information attached to each file.

Later, it was not possible to see it, as the clarity of dawn prevented it.

I would greatly appreciate your assistance in clarifying this matter, and I hope not to

"We have wasted their valuable time." The original document was attached to the digital folder of the case with the name "Observation Report."

Along with the report, a total of 13 photographic files were entered, with the stand-out photos being 20231005_060422.jpg and 20231005_062936.jpg, and a letter containing the aforementioned report.

The user's location was georeferenced at the coordinates 32° 21’ 10” S,

70° 32’46” W and 851 m.s.n.m., in the commune of Lo Barnechea, Metropolitan Region of Santiago (Figure 1).

Investigation:

                                                      Figure 1

                 The study subject was the photograph: 20231005_060422.jpg (Figure 2).
                                       Figure 2

The file supporting the report was digitally perited, confirming it had not been altered. The metadata information reveals the following parameters:

that the capture was performed on 05-10-2023 at 06:04:22 HL, an image size
of 4000 x 1800 pixels, captured at 72dpi, exposure time 1/4 second. The aperture
was f/1.8 and the ISO 2500. The main camera of a Samsung SM-A336M smartphone
was used and the resulting image was stored as a JPG file.

After consulting the astronomical scenario at the time of capture, it was possible
to verify the following situation shown in Figure 3. In it, the planet Venus and the
star Regulus are located near the azimut 70°.

Figure 3

The following image shows the similarity of positions between what was reported and the astronomical scenario at the time of capture (Figure 4).

                                      Figure 4

Additionally, the image 20231005_062936 was taken, also reported as it appears in (Figure 5).

                                      Figure 5

The previous photograph is consistent with the possibility of optical aberration.

It occurs when the camera processor exerts a great effort to achieve focus in extreme conditions. More information can be found in the following URL where a forced focus on the moon resulted in the rings observed (Figure 6).

Figure 6

Based on the analysis of the testimony and the results of forensic, geographical, photographic, air traffic, and astronomical studies, it was concluded that the reported sighting was genuine.

Conclusion: it is consistent with the location of the planet Venus and the star Regulus (Cor Leonis-Rex-Kabeleced-Al Kalb al Asad) in the constellation IUA: Leo. Both located near 70° and congruent with what the user indicated.
